clue.text: Energy from northern Germany consumed by outfit in the past

parts.note: a getup is a set of clothes, an outfit

indicators.note: the pair of letters is swallowed up by the word for 'in the past', so they sit inside it

parts.note: ago means in the past, as in 'years ago'
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: A burst of vigour once came from an outfit worn in northern Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed by' signals a container: Germany's letter is its international car code, D for Deutschland.
explanation.definitionFit: Get-up-and-go is an informal noun for drive, vigour and enthusiasm.

clue.text: Artist unknown in Indian territory

indicators.note: the unknown letter is placed inside the name of the territory

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast, once a Portuguese territory
Y is an algebraic unknown, like x and z

explanation.surface: An unidentified painter turns up somewhere in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was a celebrated Spanish painter, so he is an artist by example.

clue.text: Make a big thing of brass instrument

definitions.meaning: to proclaim it loudly, boasting about it
a valved brass instrument with a bright tone

explanation.surface: Someone is told to make a fuss of a brass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means proclaim or boast about; as a noun it names a brass instrument.

clue.text: Homer might be among one's passions

definitions.text: Homer might be among one's passions

parts.words: Homer might be among one's passions
parts.note: a homer is a homing pigeon, so this person's hobby involves breeding and racing such birds

explanation.surface: Somebody counts the Greek poet Homer among their great loves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer' looks like the poet, but with a small h it is a homing pigeon; the capital letter only comes from its position at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps and races homing birds as a hobby is said to fancy them.

clue.text: No time left to tour Scottish island? That's fanciful

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go round it, so these letters surround the island

parts.note: taken as written
Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast

explanation.surface: Someone says there is no time remaining for a trip round a Scottish island, calling the idea unrealistic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something notional exists only as an idea, so it is imaginary or speculative.

clue.text: Greek getting behind corruption

parts.note: aft means at or towards the back, behind

explanation.surface: A Greek person is involved in bribery and backhanders.
explanation.definitionFit: Graft is the use of political office for dishonest personal gain, a form of corruption.

clue.text: Unrestrained Irish wit's broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard, so the surname is taken as it sounds

parts.note: Oscar Wilde was the Dublin-born playwright famed for his wit

explanation.surface: An unrestrained Irish humorist has his jokes transmitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild behaviour is uncontrolled, so the word is a synonym for unrestrained.

clue.text: Outlaw in Swedish company Japanese art

indicators.note: the word for outlaw goes inside the company name

parts.note: IKEA is the Swedish flat-pack furniture firm
to outlaw something is to ban it

explanation.surface: A ban is imposed within a Swedish firm on some Japanese artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the Japanese art of formal flower arranging.

clue.text: Instrument familiar to pre-Victorians?

parts.note: the kings before Victoria were Georges, and the instrument's name sounds like a question 'did George do?', put to the Georgians

explanation.surface: An old musical instrument that people before Victoria's reign would have known.
explanation.walkthrough: The instrument's name sounds like 'did Georgie do', a phrase the Georgian era might have used; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The didgeridoo is a long wooden wind instrument played by Aboriginal Australians.

clue.text: Immature interviewer of PMs on the radio

definitions.meaning: not fully grown or developed; youthful

definitions.text: interviewer of PMs on the radio
definitions.meaning: Jimmy ... was a BBC Radio 2 presenter who interviewed several prime ministers, Margaret Thatcher among them

explanation.surface: A naive broadcaster gets to question prime ministers on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Young means youthful and so immature; Jimmy Young was a long-serving radio host known for interviewing premiers.

clue.text: Surmount cranes positioned in front of town on new day

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
the birds' letters are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: Cranes are set up on the edge of a town to overcome an obstacle on a fresh day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'positioned' is the anagram signal for 'cranes'; the birds' word, not 'in front of', supplies the scrambled letters, while 'front of town' gives just one initial.
explanation.definitionFit: To transcend is to rise above or go beyond, as one surmounts a difficulty.

clue.text: Act ruthlessly with a nightspot not reforming

indicators.note: reforming means forming anew, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Behaving ruthlessly, with a nightclub refusing to change its ways.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being prepared to do anything, however unscrupulous, to get what one wants.

clue.text: Fitting perhaps, golfer gets share at end of game

parts.note: a pro is a professional, such as the resident golfer at a club
a portion is a share or helping
taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A golf professional takes his share of the prize when the round finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something proportionate is in keeping with its context, which is one way of being suitable or apt.

clue.text: Quiz show's crooked strategist

definitions.meaning: a long-running BBC television quiz with a famous black chair
the brains behind a scheme, often a criminal plot

explanation.surface: A television quiz programme apparently has a dishonest schemer behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a BBC quiz; as a noun it also means the planner behind a crime.

clue.text: A fellow clad in rope entering vehicle — disruption to peace?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the rope-wrapped fellow goes into the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: the fellow is dressed in the rope, so the rope's letters wrap round him

parts.note: a tow is a rope used for pulling

explanation.surface: A man tied up in rope is bundled into a car, a disturbing breach of the peace.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'clad in' wraps the rope round the fellow, then 'entering' puts that bundle into the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: An act of hostility that breaks a state of peace between nations; the question mark marks understatement.

clue.text: A regulation blocking route in African country

indicators.note: to block a road is to sit in the middle of it

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London, written MI in crosswords
taken as written
a law is a regulation

explanation.surface: A rule closes off a road in some African state.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked country in south-east Africa.

clue.text: Some mutton, cold, provided in fancy gardens

indicators.note: the letter for cold is placed inside the rearranged word
fancy as an adjective means elaborate, signalling a reworking of the letters

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Some chilled lamb is served in an elegant garden setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges GARDENS into SRAGEND, with C placed after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrag end is the bony neck of mutton, a cheap cut for stewing.

clue.text: Special ability in Oriental entertainer

indicators.note: the letters are found within the run of the next two words

explanation.surface: An Eastern performer shows a particular gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural aptitude or gift for something.

clue.text: Madman in a cult that's crackers

indicators.note: crackers is slang for crazy, so these letters go haywire

explanation.surface: A deranged man belongs to a sect that is quite insane.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunatic is an insane person, the old word for a madman.

clue.text: Plan of action namely by woman taken with carnival venue

parts.note: SC abbreviates scilicet, Latin for namely
Ena is a woman's name
Rio de Janeiro hosts Brazil's famous carnival

explanation.surface: A woman specifies her travel plans to a carnival venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is a projected sequence of events, an outline of how things might go.

clue.text: School run by one heartless academic fellow

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter is dropped, keeping the outer pair

parts.note: a dean is a senior academic in a college

explanation.surface: A school is managed by a cold-hearted academic.
explanation.definitionFit: Roedean is a well-known girls' boarding school on the Sussex coast near Brighton.

clue.text: Role of armchair general in skirmish

definitions.meaning: an armchair general would picture himself directing, or running, a battle
an ongoing clash or quarrel that keeps flaring up

explanation.surface: A desk-bound strategist imagines his part in a minor fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a long continuing conflict; read literally it is the job of commanding a battle.

clue.text: Where in France good lawyer consumes cheese

indicators.note: the lawyer eats the French word, so it ends up inside

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney, a US prosecuting lawyer
ou is French for where

explanation.surface: Somewhere in France an upright lawyer eats some cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouda is a mild yellow Dutch cheese named after a town in Holland.

clue.text: Leaders in ancillary locations are sacked sadly

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Heads of support sites are sadly dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of grief, used to mean unfortunately.

clue.text: Break rule in diet strangely I once ignored

indicators.note: strangely signals the letters are arranged in an odd new order
one occurrence of the letter is left out of the mix

explanation.surface: Someone breaks a dietary rule, oddly ignoring it just this once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges RULE IN DIET; 'I once ignored' drops one of its two Is first.
explanation.definitionFit: An interlude is a pause or interval between parts of something.

clue.text: Perfect statement by one giving a hand?

parts.note: a speaker referring to himself says I, the numeral one too
to deal is to give out a hand of cards

explanation.surface: A card dealer announces his turn to give out a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means flawless, exactly as one would wish.

clue.text: Clip weed in wharf

definitions.meaning: to cut short, as a tail or someone's wages
a broad-leaved plant of the genus Rumex
an enclosed area of water where ships load and unload

explanation.surface: Someone trims the weeds growing on a quayside.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to cut short, names a common weed, and is a berth for ships.

clue.text: Secure a convenience for those letting farms

parts.note: to land something is to secure it, like a contract or fish
the gents is a men's public toilet, a convenience in British English

explanation.surface: Someone wants to obtain a toilet for farm landlords.
explanation.definitionFit: Land agents manage country estates on behalf of owners, including renting out farms to tenants.
